counterexamples.sourceReading: She says defeating him may remove any need to fight Sakura.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin postpones Sakura while prioritizing Zouken.

contexts.japanese: いい桜？　とりあえず貴女の処置は保留するわ。わたしの最優先事項は臓硯を倒す事。貴女との決着はその後よ。……ま、臓硯さえ倒してしまえば貴女と戦うこともなくなるから、うまくいけば臓硯を倒すだけでコトは済むわけだけど」
contexts.english: Okay, Sakura. We're tabling your disposal for the time being. My first priority is to defeat Zouken. I can settle things with you later... Though, once we beat Zouken, I won't need to fight you anymore, so hopefully it'll work out that way."

counterexamples.description: Rin corrects cooperation with Sakura to cooperation with Shirou.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The false start exposes the relationship tension.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin corrects cooperation with Sakura to cooperation with Shirou.

contexts.japanese: 「貴女—いえ、士郎と協力して臓硯退治をするってこと。で、そうなると離れて過ごすのは勿体ないでしょう？　だから今夜からここで生活して、士郎を鍛えることにしたの。短期間で戦力になってもらうにはスパルタしかないしね」
contexts.english: I'm helping you—no, Shirou to defeat Zouken. But it would waste a lot of time if I lived far away, right? So, I'm going to start living here from tonight, and I'll train him, too. It's going to take some spartan training to get him into fighting shape.

counterexamples.description: The schedule is new even to Shirou.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin states it smoothly as settled fact.
counterexamples.explanation: The schedule is new even to Shirou.

contexts.japanese: しれっと、俺ですら聞いた事のないスケジュールを口にする遠坂凛。
contexts.english: Rin Tohsaka starts laying out my schedule without any input from me.

counterexamples.description: Sakura begins a familial address and cuts herself off.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She switches to Tohsaka-senpai before completing it.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura begins a familial address and cuts herself off.

contexts.japanese: ね……いえ、遠坂先輩はどんな権利があってそんなコト言うんですかっ！」
contexts.english: Who gave you the right to decide that, Nee—I mean, Tohsaka-senpai!?"

counterexamples.description: Shirou's protest is casually overruled by both women.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Sakura's voice and Rin's glance erase his input.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's protest is casually overruled by both women.

contexts.japanese: 無論、俺の意見なんてのは桜の声と遠坂の一瞥であっさり却下された。
contexts.english: Of course, my opinion is completely rejected by Sakura's outcry and Tohsaka's stern glance.

counterexamples.description: Shirou calls Rin's debt explanation misleading.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He disputes presentation while accepting factual basis.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou calls Rin's debt explanation misleading.

contexts.japanese: 遠坂。その説明は、著しく誤解を招くと思うのだが。
contexts.english: Tohsaka. People are bound to get the wrong idea when you say it that way.

counterexamples.description: Shirou accepts the core truth but objects to wording.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He does not claim a magical compulsion.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou accepts the core truth but objects to wording.

contexts.japanese: 「—ああ。遠坂の発言にはところどころ反論したいんだが、言ってるコトは本当だ」
contexts.english: "...Yeah. I'm not happy about the way she makes it sound, but what she's saying is true."

counterexamples.description: Shirou remembers Rin is Sakura's older sister.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He hopes proximity will avoid conflict.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou remembers Rin is Sakura's older sister.

contexts.japanese: ……それに、遠坂は桜の姉貴なんだし。
contexts.english: Besides, Tohsaka's her big sister.

counterexamples.description: Sakura agrees because Shirou asks.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her acceptance is conditional on his position rather than enthusiasm for Rin.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura agrees because Shirou asks.

contexts.japanese: 「…………わかりました。先輩がそう言うなら、納得します」
contexts.english: "...I understand. If that's what you've decided, I'll go along with it."

counterexamples.description: Illya rejects proximity through an unnamed deictic insult.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The local household context points toward Sakura, but the source does not name her.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya rejects proximity through an unnamed deictic insult.

contexts.japanese: 「別にどこでもいいけど、そこの女の近くはイヤよ」
contexts.english: "It doesn't really matter, but not close to her."

counterexamples.description: Illya asks where the unnamed woman sleeps.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The next narration identifies her glare at Sakura.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya asks where the unnamed woman sleeps.

contexts.japanese: 一つ訊くけど、その女は何処で寝てるの」
contexts.english: Where is that woman sleeping?"

counterexamples.description: Illya sends Rin to the annex without her.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She will accept anywhere outside Sakura's location.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya sends Rin to the annex without her.

contexts.japanese: 「そう。なら離れにはリンだけでいって。離れ以外だったら、わたしはどこでもいいわ」
contexts.english: "Okay. Then Rin can stay there. I'll sleep anywhere besides the guesthouse."

counterexamples.description: Shirou aims to defeat Zouken and obtain the Grail before Sakura collapses.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The plan remains prospective.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou aims to defeat Zouken and obtain the Grail before Sakura collapses.

contexts.japanese: ……その前に臓硯を倒して聖杯を手に入れる。
contexts.english: ...I need to defeat Zouken and obtain the Holy Grail before then.

counterexamples.description: Sakura looks well but may collapse at any time.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Appearance is not cure.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura looks well but may collapse at any time.

contexts.japanese: いまは元気そうだが、いつ倒れるか判らない。
contexts.english: She seemed energetic, but she could collapse at any time.

counterexamples.description: Rider acted under Sakura's protection order.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She identifies Servant obedience as immediate basis.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider acted under Sakura's protection order.

contexts.japanese: 「……そうですね。貴方たちを運んだのは私です。サクラは貴方を守れと言った。私はサーヴァントとして、彼女の命に従ったまでです」
contexts.english: "...Yes. I carried you there. Sakura told me to protect you. I merely obeyed her order, as her Servant."

counterexamples.description: Continued use would consume Sakura's depleted energy.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rider states a prospective lethal cost.
counterexamples.explanation: Continued use would consume Sakura's depleted energy.

contexts.japanese: 「ええ。残り少ないサクラの魔力は、さらに失われたという事です。今日のように桜が私を使えば、私は桜を食い潰してしまうでしょう」
contexts.english: "Yes. Sakura has lost more of her already dwindling power. If Sakura continues to use me like she did today, I will devour her entirely."

counterexamples.description: Initial narration sees neither malice nor pity.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is Shirou's appearance-based reading before correction.
counterexamples.explanation: Initial narration sees neither malice nor pity.

contexts.japanese: 桜に対する憎しみも哀れみもない。
contexts.english: It doesn't contain any malice or pity for Sakura.

counterexamples.description: Shirou directly asks whether lost Command Spells would lead Rider to kill Sakura.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The question tests voluntary loyalty.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou directly asks whether lost Command Spells would lead Rider to kill Sakura.

contexts.japanese: 「……じゃあ訊く。ライダーは、桜が令呪をなくしたら、そのまま桜を殺すのか」
contexts.english: "...Okay, then. Would you kill Sakura if she lost all of her Command Spells?"

counterexamples.description: Rider's yes is conditional on Sakura wishing an end to suffering.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She immediately states desire for Sakura to live.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider's yes is conditional on Sakura wishing an end to suffering.

contexts.japanese: 「ええ。サクラがそれを望むのなら、私の手で楽にしようとは考えています。ですが士郎。私は、彼女の生存を望んでいる」
contexts.english: "Yes. If Sakura wishes it, I will put an end to her suffering myself. But Shirou, I want her to live."

counterexamples.description: Rider explicitly protects Sakura by choice and affection, independently of Command Spell restraint.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Command Spell restraint is irrelevant and affection is explicit.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider explicitly protects Sakura by choice and affection, independently of Command Spell restraint.

contexts.japanese: 「令呪の縛りは関係ありません。私はサクラがマスターである限り、自らの意思で彼女を守る。私は彼女が好きですから」
contexts.english: "The binding of the Command Spells has nothing to do with it. As long as Sakura is my Master, I will protect her of my own will. Because I am fond of her."

counterexamples.description: Rider says silence does not prevent mutual understanding.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shared reticence and resemblance ground intimacy.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider says silence does not prevent mutual understanding.

contexts.japanese: もともと饒舌ではないのですから、会話がないのも当然でしょう。そのような物がなくとも、私たちはお互いをよく解っています」
contexts.english: Neither of us are talkative, so it stands to reason that conversations do not happen. But even without it, we understand each other."

counterexamples.description: Shirou has heard what happened but refuses to claim lived understanding.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Information and understanding are separated.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou has heard what happened but refuses to claim lived understanding.

contexts.japanese: いや、言峰の口からどんなものだったかはとっくに聞いている。
contexts.english: Though, I've already heard from Kotomine's lips what happened to her.

counterexamples.description: Shirou rejects saying he understands easily.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Even plausible imagination does not authorize the claim.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou rejects saying he understands easily.

contexts.japanese: だが—それは俺が、容易く“解る”なんて口にしてはいけない事だ。
contexts.english: Still...I could never claim to understand what Sakura's been through.

counterexamples.description: Rider's hypothetical killing is tied to glib claimed understanding.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No present attack occurs.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider's hypothetical killing is tied to glib claimed understanding.

contexts.japanese: 「でしょうね。サクラは貴方に知られないように努めてきた。その貴方がここで解るなどと口にすれば、私は貴方を殺している」
contexts.english: "Indeed. Sakura has been trying not to let you know. If you claimed that you understood it, then I would have killed you."

counterexamples.description: Rider trusts Shirou's core despite immaturity.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her approval is qualified rather than wholesale praise.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider trusts Shirou's core despite immaturity.

contexts.japanese: 貴方は未熟で不器用ですが、その芯にあるものは信用に足ります。だからこそ、サクラにとって貴方は救いだったのでしょう」
contexts.english: You are clumsy and inexperienced, but trustworthy at your core. That is how you have saved Sakura."

counterexamples.description: Pain and suffering remain the largest restored emotions.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The paradox coexists with Shirou as salvation.
counterexamples.explanation: Pain and suffering remain the largest restored emotions.

contexts.japanese: その中で最も大きかったのは痛みと苦しみですが、それでも諦めるだけだった彼女にとって、貴方は唯一確かな救いだったのです」
contexts.english: Pain and suffering were the greatest among them, but to someone who has only ever known despair, you were her one and only salvation."

counterexamples.description: Shirou cannot relate to Sakura's suffering or explain her love.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His epistemic humility continues.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou cannot relate to Sakura's suffering or explain her love.

contexts.japanese: 桜が何を思い、何に苦しんできたかを共有できない俺には、俺を好きになってくれた理由さえ判らない。
contexts.english: I don't know why she came to love me, when she's suffered on a level that I could never possibly relate to.

counterexamples.description: Rider speaks with quiet sadness and gratitude.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The affect complicates her message about happiness.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider speaks with quiet sadness and gratitude.

contexts.japanese: 静かな悲しみと感謝を込めてそう言った。
contexts.english: Her voice contains quiet sadness and gratitude.

counterexamples.description: Rider claims Sakura wants nothing beyond Shirou's presence.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The claim remains Rider's speech, not neutral omniscient fact.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider claims Sakura wants nothing beyond Shirou's presence.

contexts.japanese: サクラの幸福は、貴方が生きて傍にいてくれる、という事。それ以外に彼女が望むものなどない」
contexts.english: What makes Sakura happy is having you by her side. She does not wish for anything else."

counterexamples.description: Shirou recognizes his fighting threatens Sakura's happiness.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The contradiction is explicit before he grips his arm.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou recognizes his fighting threatens Sakura's happiness.

contexts.japanese: 間桐桜にとって、衛宮士郎が戦うという事自体が、彼女の幸福を脅かしている。
contexts.english: To Sakura Matou, Shirou Emiya fighting this war is a threat to her happiness.

counterexamples.description: Shirou insists he must fight if still capable.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Condition and bodily cost remain.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou insists he must fight if still capable.

contexts.japanese: どんな身体だろうとまだ戦えるのなら、戦わないといけない。
contexts.english: If I can still fight, then I have to, no matter what shape I'm in.

counterexamples.description: His motive has shifted from ending war to Sakura alone.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The identity crisis follows this chosen commitment.
counterexamples.explanation: His motive has shifted from ending war to Sakura alone.

contexts.japanese: 戦いを止める為ではなく、桜の為だけに戦うと決めてしまった。
contexts.english: I decided that I'd fight for her sake now, not to end the war.

counterexamples.description: Rider's question includes whatever may happen.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The condition is deliberately broad and ominous.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider's question includes whatever may happen.

contexts.japanese: この先に、たとえ何があったとしても」
contexts.english: No matter what happens from now on?"

counterexamples.description: Shirou thinks he ought to nod firmly.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is obligation/intention, not a completed nod.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou thinks he ought to nod firmly.

contexts.japanese: なら、迷いもなく頷いてライダーに応えなくてはいけない。
contexts.english: I have to nod firmly.

counterexamples.description: Shirou cannot say the answer aloud.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He partly understands the condition's implication.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou cannot say the answer aloud.

contexts.japanese: そう解っていても、はっきりと気持ちを口に出来なかった。
contexts.english: I know that, but I can't say it out loud.

counterexamples.description: The Grail is imagined capable of other wishes.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Sakura's happiness is set apart in the damaged next entry.
counterexamples.explanation: The Grail is imagined capable of other wishes.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯を手に入れれば、他のどんな望みも叶う。
contexts.english: With the Holy Grail, I could make any other wish come true.

counterexamples.description: The shared view places Shirou and Illya about five meters from Rin and Archer.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The spatial tableau precedes the Shadow expansion.
counterexamples.explanation: The shared view places Shirou and Illya about five meters from Rin and Archer.

contexts.japanese: そこから五メートルほど離れた場所に、銀髪の少女と、手を繋いで立ち尽くす衛宮士郎の姿があった。
contexts.english: Five meters away from them stands a silver-haired girl holding hands with Shirou Emiya.

counterexamples.description: The Shadow contracts then expands through a pufferfish image.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The grotesque comparison is visual and sequential.
counterexamples.explanation: The Shadow contracts then expands through a pufferfish image.

contexts.japanese: 影は枯れ木のように縮んだあと、河豚のように膨れ上がった。
contexts.english: It shrinks like a withered tree, and then expands like a pufferfish.

counterexamples.description: The compressed account says Archer dies protecting Rin.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This retrospective statement is preserved for reconciliation with the extended action scene.
counterexamples.explanation: The compressed account says Archer dies protecting Rin.

contexts.japanese: 赤い騎士は遠坂凛を庇って絶命し、衛宮士郎は、幸運にも助かった。
contexts.english: The red knight dies protecting Rin Tohsaka, and Shirou Emiya is saved by sheer luck.

counterexamples.description: Only Shirou's protruding left arm misses the sheltering luck.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The sentence anticipates the loss without describing voluntary sacrifice.
counterexamples.explanation: Only Shirou's protruding left arm misses the sheltering luck.

contexts.japanese: ただ、窪みから出ていた左腕だけは、その幸運に与れずに—
contexts.english: But his exposed left arm was not so lucky...

counterexamples.description: Sakura had shared Rider's perception from the Emiya house.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The preceding images are a real remote view, not an unreal dream.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura had shared Rider's perception from the Emiya house.

contexts.japanese: 衛宮邸からでも様子が判るようにと、サーヴァントと視界を共有していた間桐桜は、その光景で現実に引き戻された。
contexts.english: Sakura had been sharing her Servant's perception so that she could keep an eye on things from the Emiya house. The shocking scene jolted her back to reality.

counterexamples.description: Half a day has passed since Rider was sent as escort.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The duration frames Sakura's waiting.
counterexamples.explanation: Half a day has passed since Rider was sent as escort.

contexts.japanese: ライダーを士郎の護衛に送ってから半日。
contexts.english: It's been half a day since she sent Rider to protect Shirou.

counterexamples.description: Nausea brings stomach contents to Sakura's throat.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The bodily reaction follows abrupt sensory separation.
counterexamples.explanation: Nausea brings stomach contents to Sakura's throat.

contexts.japanese: 喉元まで、胃の中のモノが戻ってきた。
contexts.english: The contents of her stomach rise to her throat.

counterexamples.description: Sakura runs to the changing room and sink.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The staging remains domestic and immediate.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura runs to the changing room and sink.

contexts.japanese: 脱衣場に駆け込む。
contexts.english: She runs to the changing room.

counterexamples.description: Her hair hides her face from the mirror.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The mirror image is deferred until the later contradiction.
counterexamples.explanation: Her hair hides her face from the mirror.

contexts.japanese: 長い髪はカーテンのように揺れて、鏡から顔を隠す。
contexts.english: Her long hair sways like a curtain, concealing her face from the mirror.

counterexamples.description: Sakura explicitly judges Rider's images real.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Calling the experience a nightmare does not negate events.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura explicitly judges Rider's images real.

contexts.japanese: ……あの映像に間違いはない。
contexts.english: ...Those images were real.

counterexamples.description: Shirou protected the silver-haired girl and lost the left arm.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The viewpoint does not confuse Illya with Sakura.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou protected the silver-haired girl and lost the left arm.

contexts.japanese: 衛宮士郎は銀髪の少女を庇って、左腕を影に呑まれた。
contexts.english: Shirou Emiya protected the silver-haired girl, and the Shadow swallowed his arm.

counterexamples.description: Chills and exultation coexist in Sakura.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The troubling positive affect is not sanitized.
counterexamples.explanation: Chills and exultation coexist in Sakura.

contexts.japanese: 背中には悪寒と妙な高揚感があって、何が起きたのか、何をするべきなのかも考えつかない。
contexts.english: She feels both chills and a strange sense of exultation, and can't quite process what happened or what she should do next.

counterexamples.description: Sakura knows only that she hates herself.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Self-loathing follows opposed reactions.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura knows only that she hates herself.

contexts.japanese: 分かるのは、自分が嫌いだという事だけだ。
contexts.english: All she knows for sure is that she hates herself.

counterexamples.description: Sakura recognizes incapacitating injury would solve nothing.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The fantasy is repudiated before causation is misstated.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura recognizes incapacitating injury would solve nothing.

contexts.japanese: そんなコトはなんの解決にもならない。
contexts.english: It wouldn't solve anything.

counterexamples.description: The actual wound threatens Shirou's life.
counterexamples.sourceReading: It exceeds confinement to the house.
counterexamples.explanation: The actual wound threatens Shirou's life.

contexts.japanese: 外に出られないどころか、命に関わる傷を負った。
contexts.english: His life was in danger, never mind his ability to leave the house.

counterexamples.description: Retching continues after the stomach is empty.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The reaction is prolonged rather than a single vomit.
counterexamples.explanation: Retching continues after the stomach is empty.

contexts.japanese: 胃の中のものを全て吐き出しても嘔吐は止まらない。
contexts.english: She's already vomited everything in her stomach, but the retching won't stop.

counterexamples.description: Pain is interpreted by Sakura as punishment.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The narration attributes the interpretation to her.
counterexamples.explanation: Pain is interpreted by Sakura as punishment.

contexts.japanese: 切り刻まれるような腹部の痛みと喉の傷は、自らを責める罰のようだ、と彼女は思った。
contexts.english: It's almost as if the mangling pain in her stomach and the searing in her throat are meant to punish her, she thinks to herself.

counterexamples.description: Tens of minutes pass before nausea subsides.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The duration is substantial.
counterexamples.explanation: Tens of minutes pass before nausea subsides.

contexts.japanese: ……そうして数十分後。
contexts.english: ...Several dozen minutes pass.

counterexamples.description: The marathon comparison describes exhaustion.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No literal distance is traveled.
counterexamples.explanation: The marathon comparison describes exhaustion.

contexts.japanese: 何十キロと続くマラソンをやり終えた後のように、両手を洗面台につけて息を整え、
contexts.english: She grips the sink in both hands, trying to catch her breath like she's just finished running a marathon.

counterexamples.description: Sakura admits with rapture that Shirou can no longer fight.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Relief survives guilt and bodily punishment.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura admits with rapture that Shirou can no longer fight.

contexts.japanese: 「—でもこれで、もう先輩は戦えない」
contexts.english: "...Now Senpai can't fight anymore."

counterexamples.description: Sakura's wish for Shirou's safety is explicitly sincere.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her concern is genuine despite the damaged contradictory smile entry.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura's wish for Shirou's safety is explicitly sincere.

contexts.japanese: 彼女は本気で、一点の偽りもなく、衛宮士郎の無事を願う。
contexts.english: She sincerely and earnestly wishes for his safety.

counterexamples.description: Sakura cannot oppose Zouken in Kirei/Shirou's current assessment.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is why victory appears decided.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura cannot oppose Zouken in Kirei/Shirou's current assessment.

contexts.japanese: ……本来なら残った二人が戦うべきなのだが、桜は臓硯に逆らえない。そういった意味で、勝敗はもう決まっているようなものだった。
contexts.english: ...Normally, the last survivors would fight, but Sakura can't disobey Zouken. In that sense, he's already won.

counterexamples.description: Kirei predicts Zouken will retrieve or dispose of Sakura.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He says prevention is difficult and offers no duty/benefit.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei predicts Zouken will retrieve or dispose of Sakura.

contexts.japanese: 「間桐臓硯としては間桐桜を取り戻すか、始末するかのどちらかだろう。これを防ぐのは難しく、おまえたちには防ぐ義務もない。なにしろ間桐臓硯を倒したところで、おまえたちに益はないからな」

contexts.english: Fuji-nee nods.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page10:1
contexts.japanese: 「はいどうぞ。とろろ汁に使うんですか？」
contexts.english: "Here you go. Are you going to use it for your yam soup?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page10:1
contexts.japanese: つー、と白いとろろに醤油をかける。
contexts.english: A line of soy sauce streams from the bottle onto the grated white mound.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page10:1
contexts.japanese: ぐりぐりとかき回した後、ごはんにかけて一口。
contexts.english: I stir the mixture up, pour it over my rice, and take a bite.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page11:1
contexts.japanese: うむ、このすり下ろされた山芋の粘つき加減と、自己主張の激し過ぎる強烈な醤油の辛さがまた—
contexts.english: Mmm. The stickiness of the grated yam combined with the intense flavor of the soy sauce...

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page11:1
contexts.japanese: 「ごぶっ……！　うわまず、これソースだぞソース！　しかもオイスター！」
contexts.english: "(Cough)! What the...!? This isn't soy sauce! It's...it's...oyster sauce!"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page12:1
contexts.japanese: 「くく、あはははははは！」
contexts.english: "Heh..ahahahahaha!!!"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page12:1
contexts.japanese: ばさり、と勢いよく新聞紙を投げ捨てる藤ねえ。
contexts.english: Fuji-nee tosses her newspaper onto the table with an enthusiastic flick of her wrists.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 「どうだ、朝のうちにソースとお醤油のラベルを取り替えておく作戦なのだー！」
contexts.english: "What'd you think of my little stunt switching the oyster sauce and soy sauce labels first thing in the morning!?"

counterexamples.description: Taiga thanks Sakura, warns both students about lateness and remains an incongruous teacher.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The scene does not assert that either student is already late.
counterexamples.explanation: Taiga thanks Sakura, warns both students about lateness and remains an incongruous teacher.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page17:1
contexts.japanese: 「はい、ごちそうさま。朝ごはん、今日もおいしかったよ桜ちゃん」
contexts.english: "Thanks for the meal! Breakfast was great as usual, Sakura."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page17:1
contexts.japanese: 「それじゃあ先に行くわね。二人とも、遅刻したら怒るわよー」
contexts.english: "And now I'm heading off! You two will be in trouble if you're late for school!"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page18:1
contexts.japanese: ……アレでうちの学校の教師だっていうんだから、世の中ほんと間違っている。
contexts.english: There's something terribly wrong with a world that allows someone like her to be a teacher.

counterexamples.description: Sakura connects the prank to Shirou's nickname offense, crying Taiga and the resulting study hall.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Yesterday's classroom disruption is not reassigned to the current morning.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura connects the prank to Shirou's nickname offense, crying Taiga and the resulting study hall.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page19:1
contexts.japanese: 「いえ、そういうのではなくて……あの、昨日藤村先生に何かしたんですか？　食べ物に細工するなんて、藤村先生にしてはやりすぎですから」
contexts.english: "No, it's not that. Um...what did you do to Ms. Fujimura yesterday? She wouldn't usually go so far as to mess with someone's meal."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 「ん……いや、それがさ。昨日、ついアダ名で呼んじまった」
contexts.english: "Hm. Well, I accidentally called her by her nickname."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 「それじゃあ仕方ありませんね。先輩、藤村先生に謝らなかったんでしょう？」
contexts.english: "Well I guess there's no avoiding her getting angry again. And you didn't apologize?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 「面目ない。いつものコトなんで忘れてた」
contexts.english: "Sorry. I forgot, but only because that kind of stuff happens all the time."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page21:1
contexts.japanese: 「だめですよ。藤村先生、先輩にあだ名を言われるのだけは嫌がるんですから。また泣かせちゃったんでしょう」
contexts.english: "Still not good. You know how much Ms. Fujimura hates being called by her nickname. You made her cry again, didn't you?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page21:1
contexts.japanese: 「……泣かした上に脱兎の如く走り去らせた。おかげで昨日の英語は自習だった」
contexts.english: "Not only did I make her cry, she also ran away like a scared rabbit. And thanks to that incident, yesterday's English class ended up being a study hall."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page21:1
contexts.japanese: そして俺はみんなからルーズリーフで作られた学生名誉賞を受賞したが、そんなものは当然ゴミ箱に捨てた。
contexts.english: In fact, everyone in class worked together to make an award for me from their notebook paper because of that. I threw it away, obviously.

counterexamples.description: Sakura sides with Taiga as an older-sister figure; Shirou moves from freeloader complaint to gratitude after Kiritsugu's death.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Both irritation and dependence remain.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura sides with Taiga as an older-sister figure; Shirou moves from freeloader complaint to gratitude after Kiritsugu's death.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page22:1
contexts.japanese: 「もう。それじゃ今朝のは先輩が悪いです」
contexts.english: "Oh my. Sounds like you brought that on yourself then, Senpai."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page22:1
contexts.japanese: 桜にとっても藤ねえは姉貴みたいなもんだから、基本的に藤ねえの味方なのだ。
contexts.english: Fuji-nee is like an older sister to Sakura, so she's typically on Fuji-nee's side.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page22:1
contexts.japanese: それはそれで嬉しいのだが、藤ねえの相手を四六時中しているこっちの身にもなってほしい。
contexts.english: Which is fine on its own, but I wish she would consider the fact that I have to deal with Fuji-nee all day long.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page23:1
contexts.japanese: もともと藤ねえは切嗣の知り合いで、俺が養子に貰われた頃からこの家に入り浸っていた人だ。
contexts.english: Fuji-nee was originally an acquaintance of my old man, and she's swung by the house pretty frequently since I was adopted.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page23:1
contexts.japanese: 親父が他界してからも頻繁に顔を出すようになって、今では朝飯と晩飯をうちで食べていく、という見事なまでの居候ぶりを示している。
contexts.english: She kept on coming over even after my old man died, and now she acts like a freeloader, eating breakfast and dinner every day.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page24:1
contexts.japanese: —いや。
contexts.english: Actually...

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page24:1
contexts.japanese: そんな藤ねえがいたから、親父が死んでからも一人でやってこれたのかもしれない。
contexts.english: It might have been thanks to Fuji-nee that I was able to make it on my own after my old man died.

counterexamples.description: The news separates observed casualties, the gas-leak account, construction rumor and Shirou's concern for hundreds.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Neither death nor the later supernatural cause is imported.
counterexamples.explanation: The news separates observed casualties, the gas-leak account, construction rumor and Shirou's concern for hundreds.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page27:1
contexts.japanese: 朝食を済ませて、登校の支度をする。
contexts.english: I finish breakfast and get ready for school.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page27:1
contexts.japanese: テレビから流れるニュースを聞きながら、桜と一緒に食器を片づける。
contexts.english: I put away the dishes with Sakura as I listen to the news on TV in the background.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page28:1
contexts.japanese: 桜はぼんやりとテレビを眺めていた。
contexts.english: Sakura is looking blankly at the TV.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page28:1
contexts.japanese: 画面には“ガス漏れ事故、連続”と大げさなテロップが打ち出されている。
contexts.english: A flashy caption reading "Gas Leaks Continue" pops up on the screen.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page29:1
contexts.japanese: ガス漏れによる事故とされているが、同じような事故がここのところ頻発している。
contexts.english: Authorities have been calling it an accident resulting from gas leaks, but for some reason these incidents have been happening often.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page30:1
contexts.japanese: 「今のニュース、気になるのか桜」
contexts.english: "Are you worried about the incident, Sakura?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page30:1
contexts.japanese: 「え—いえ、別に。ただ事故が新都で起きているなら近いなあって。……先輩、新都の方でアルバイトしていますよね？」
contexts.english: "Eh...well, not really. I was just thinking that this happened in Shinto, which is very close to us. Senpai, your part-time job is in Shinto, right?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page30:1
contexts.japanese: 「してるけど、別にそんな大きな店じゃないよ。今のニュースみたいな事故は起きないと思う」
contexts.english: "Yeah, but the shop's not that big. I don't think an accident like that would happen there."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page31:1
contexts.japanese: ガス漏れならどんな建物でも起きるものだし、なにより数百人もの人間が被害にあっている、というのは胸に痛い。
contexts.english: Gas leaks can happen in any building, and it especially pains me to think that hundreds of people have fallen victim.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page32:1
contexts.japanese: 同じような事故が頻発しているのは、新都を急開発した時に欠陥工事をしたからだ、なんて話もあがっているとか。
contexts.english: Some say that these accidents are happening because of faulty construction work done during the rapid development projects in Shinto.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page32:1
contexts.japanese: 真偽はどうであれ、これ以上の犠牲者は出てほしくないというのが正直な気持ちだが—
contexts.english: Either way, I hope there won't be any more victims.

counterexamples.description: Sakura answers broad public danger with her twice-checked gas valve, and Shirou identifies the mismatch.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No hidden motive is supplied.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura answers broad public danger with her twice-checked gas valve, and Shirou identifies the mismatch.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page33:1
contexts.japanese: 「……物騒な話だ。俺たちも気をつけないと」
contexts.english: "It's a disturbing story. We need to be careful too."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page33:1
contexts.japanese: 「あ、それならご心配なく先輩。ガスの元栓はいつも二回チェックしてますから安心です」
contexts.english: "Well don't worry about that, Senpai. I always make sure to check that the gas is turned off properly. Twice."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page34:1
contexts.japanese: 「いや、そういう話でなくて」
contexts.english: "No, that's not my point."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page34:1
contexts.japanese: ……うん。前から思っていたけど、桜も微妙にズレてるな。
contexts.english: Yep. I've always known Sakura is a little off, too.

counterexamples.description: The pair coordinate locks, return times, dinner preparation and morning-practice haste.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Sakura and Taiga's spare keys and the last-person rule remain explicit.
counterexamples.explanation: The pair coordinate locks, return times, dinner preparation and morning-practice haste.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page35:1
contexts.japanese: 「先輩、裏手の戸締まりはしました？」
contexts.english: "Senpai, did you lock the back door?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page35:1
contexts.japanese: 「したよ。閂かけたけど、問題あるか？」
contexts.english: "I bolted it. Is that a problem?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page36:1
contexts.japanese: 「わたしはいつも通りです。たぶんわたしの方が早いと思いますから、夕食の下準備は済ませておきますね」
contexts.english: "I should be back at the usual time. I think I will be back before you, so I'll make preparations for dinner."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page36:1
contexts.japanese: 「……ん、助かる。俺も出来るだけ早く帰るよ」
contexts.english: "Yeah, that'll be great. I'll try to come home as soon as possible too."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page37:1
contexts.japanese: がちゃり、と門に鍵をかける。
contexts.english: The gate is locked tight.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page37:1
contexts.japanese: 桜と藤ねえはうちの合い鍵を持っていて、戸締りは最後に出る人間がする決まりだ。
contexts.english: Sakura and Fuji-nee both have keys to the house, and the rule is that whoever leaves last is in charge of locking everything up.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page37:1
contexts.japanese: 「行こうか。急がないと朝練に間に合わない」
contexts.english: "Let's go. You'll be late for morning practice if you don't hurry."

counterexamples.description: The hilltop house, residential area, central intersection and branching destinations remain broadly legible.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Bridge, temple, opposite housing, shops and school are alternatives from the intersection.
counterexamples.explanation: The hilltop house, residential area, central intersection and branching destinations remain broadly legible.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page38:1
contexts.japanese: 桜と一緒に町へ歩き出す。
contexts.english: Sakura and I walk into town.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page38:1
contexts.japanese: 衛宮の家は坂の上にあって、町の中心地とは離れている。
contexts.english: The Emiya house is located on top of a hill, away from the center of town.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page39:1
contexts.japanese: こうして坂を下りていけば住宅地に出て、さらに下りていくと、
contexts.english: Heading down the hill leads us to the residential area.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page39:1
contexts.japanese: 町の中心地である交差点に出る。
contexts.english: Going further down, we reach the intersection at the center of town.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page40:1
contexts.japanese: ここから隣町に通じる大橋、
contexts.english: Several roads lead out from the center of town: there's a large bridge that connects to the neighboring town,

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page40:1
contexts.japanese: 柳洞寺に続く坂道、
contexts.english: a hill that leads to Ryudou Temple,

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page40:1
contexts.japanese: うちとは反対側にある住宅地、
contexts.english: a residential area located opposite my house,

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page40:1
contexts.japanese: いつも桜と自分がお世話になってる商店街、
contexts.english: a shopping district that both Sakura and I often go to,

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page40:1
contexts.japanese: 最後にこれから向かう学校と、様々な分岐がある。
contexts.english: and finally, there's a path that leads to our school.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page41:1
contexts.japanese: 寄り道をせず学校へ向かう。
contexts.english: We head straight to school without taking any detours.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page41:1
contexts.japanese: まだ七時になったばかり、という事で通学路に人気はない。
contexts.english: It's barely seven o'clock, so there's hardly anyone around.

counterexamples.description: Sakura unusually delays going to kyudo, invites Shirou to the dojo and retreats apologetically after his Issei obligation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her reason remains unexplained to Shirou.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura unusually delays going to kyudo, invites Shirou to the dojo and retreats apologetically after his Issei obligation.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page42:1
contexts.japanese: 「それじゃまたな。部活、がんばれよ」
contexts.english: "See you later. Good luck at practice."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page42:1
contexts.japanese: 桜は弓道部に所属しているので、朝はここで別れる事になる。
contexts.english: Sakura's in the kyudou club, so this is where we usually split off.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page43:1
セイバールート一日目-06:page43:1
contexts.japanese: というのに。
contexts.english: And yet...

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page43:1
contexts.japanese: 今朝にかぎって、桜は弓道場へ向かおうとはしなかった。
contexts.english: Sakura doesn't budge this morning.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page44:1
contexts.japanese: 「桜？　体の調子、悪いのか」
contexts.english: "Sakura? Are you not feeling well or something?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page45:1
contexts.japanese: 「いや、別に道場に用はないぞ。それに今日は一成に頼まれてるから、生徒会室に行かないとまずい」
contexts.english: "Well, I don't really have any business at the dojo. Besides, Issei asked me to do something, so I need to go to the student council room."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page46:1
contexts.japanese: 「……そ、そうですよね。ごめんなさい、余計なことを言っちゃって」
contexts.english: "I-I suppose you're right. I'm sorry for bringing it up."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page46:1
contexts.japanese: ぺこり、と頭をさげる桜。
contexts.english: Sakura quickly bows her head.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page47:1
contexts.japanese: 「それじゃあ失礼します。晩ご飯、楽しみにしていてくださいね」
contexts.english: "I'll be going, then. Please look forward to dinner tonight."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page47:1
contexts.japanese: 桜は申し訳なさそうに道場へ走り去っていった。
contexts.english: Sakura runs towards the dojo, seeming almost apologetic.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page47:1
contexts.english: "What was that?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-06:page47:1
contexts.japanese: はて。今のは一体どんな意味があったんだろう……？
contexts.english: I wonder what that was all about...

counterexamples.description: The late hour, empty streets and Shirou's decision to begin escorting Sakura remain connected without claiming he has already done so.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Sakura's home remains on the opposite side of town from the Emiya house.
counterexamples.explanation: The late hour, empty streets and Shirou's decision to begin escorting Sakura remain connected without claiming he has already done so.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page0:1
contexts.japanese: 時刻は七時半頃だろう。
contexts.english: It's about half past seven.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page0:1
contexts.japanese: この時間ならぽつぽつと人通りがあってもいいのに、外には人気というものがなかった。
contexts.english: There should still be people out and about at this hour, but there are no signs of anyone around.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page3:1
contexts.japanese: 「……ガス漏れに強盗か。物騒な事になってきたな」
contexts.english: "Gas leaks and burglars, huh? Seems like it's getting dangerous around here."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page3:1
contexts.japanese: これじゃあ夜に出歩こう、なんて人が減るのも当然だ。
contexts.english: No wonder people are avoiding walking around at night.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page3:1
contexts.japanese: 桜を一人で帰らせるのも危なくなってきた。
contexts.english: It's probably not safe to let Sakura go home on her own anymore.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page3:1
contexts.japanese: 藤ねえはともかく、桜の家は反対側の住宅地にある。
contexts.english: Fuji-nee might be fine, but Sakura's house is in the residential area on the other side of town.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page3:1
contexts.japanese: 今日からでも夜は送っていかなくては—
contexts.english: Guess I should walk her home starting toni—

counterexamples.description: Sakura and Taiga are already eating; Shirou washes, changes and joins them after Sakura prepares his portion.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His bedroom remains distinct from the storehouse.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura and Taiga are already eating; Shirou washes, changes and joins them after Sakura prepares his portion.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page9:1
contexts.japanese: 坂を上がりきって我が家に到着する。
contexts.english: I climb up the hill and reach my house.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page9:1
contexts.japanese: 家の明かりが点いているのを見ると、桜と藤ねえはもう帰ってきているようだ。
contexts.english: The lights are already on, which means Sakura and Fuji-nee are home.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page10:1
contexts.japanese: 居間に入るなり、旨そうなメシの匂い。
contexts.english: The moment I step into the living room, I smell the delicious aroma of dinner.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page10:1
contexts.japanese: テーブルには夕食中の桜と藤ねえの姿がある。
contexts.english: Sakura and Fuji-nee are both eating at the table.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page10:1
contexts.japanese: 今晩の主菜はチキンのクリーム煮らしく、ホワイトソース系が大好きな藤ねえはご機嫌だ。
contexts.english: Tonight's meal is chicken stewed in cream sauce, and it's put Fuji-nee in an especially good mood.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-07:page11:1
contexts.japanese: 「お帰りなさい先輩。お先に失礼していますね」
contexts.english: "Welcome home, Senpai. Please excuse us for eating ahead of you."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-13:page11:1
contexts.japanese: 「だめだよ、そんなの本末転倒じゃないか。女の子が夜出歩くから危ないっていうのに、さらに女の子を増やして—」
contexts.english: "That really doesn't fix anything. My concern is that a girl's walking alone at night, so adding another girl would be—"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-13:page11:1
contexts.english: ...Wait a minute.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-13:page11:1
contexts.japanese: 目の前の藤ねえを女の子と呼ぶのは語弊がある。
contexts.english: Calling Fuji-nee a girl may be a bit of a misnomer.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-13:page12:1
contexts.japanese: 「できるよー？　だから桜ちゃんを送っていくのも問題なし。それでいい、桜ちゃん？」
contexts.english: "Of course I can. And that's why walking Sakura home is not a problem. Are you good with it, Sakura?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-13:page12:1
contexts.japanese: 「決まりだね。それじゃ行こっか。わたしも今日はそろそろ帰ろうかなって思ってたんだ」
contexts.english: "That settles it. Let's get going. I was just thinking I should go home, too."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-13:page12:1
contexts.japanese: 桜の手を取って歩き出す藤ねえ。
contexts.english: Fuji-nee takes Sakura's hand and starts to leave.

counterexamples.description: Shirou stops Sakura to praise dinner; she beams, and he blushes at the change in how he perceives her.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The scene does not establish a relationship.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou stops Sakura to praise dinner; she beams, and he blushes at the change in how he perceives her.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-13:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 「あ、ちょっと待った。桜」
contexts.english: "Oh, hold on a minute, Sakura."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-13:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 「？　なんですか、先輩？」
contexts.english: "What is it, Senpai?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-13:page13:1
セイバールート一日目-13:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 満面の笑顔でそう言って、桜は居間を後にした。
contexts.english: Sakura beams and leaves the living room.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-13:page14:1
contexts.japanese: 自分の頬が赤くなっているのが判る。
contexts.english: I can tell my cheeks are burning red.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-13:page14:1
contexts.japanese: ……本当に、最近の桜は不意打ちが多くて困る。
contexts.english: Honestly, Sakura takes me by surprise a lot lately. It's...perplexing.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-13:page15:1
contexts.japanese: ……情けないな、俺。
contexts.english: I'm so pathetic.

counterexamples.description: This branch keeps Shirou's decision to escort Sakura despite her concern about rest and Shinji.
counterexamples.sourceReading: It remains distinct from the Taiga-escort branch.
counterexamples.explanation: This branch keeps Shirou's decision to escort Sakura despite her concern about rest and Shinji.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page0:1
contexts.japanese: 夕食を作ってもらったお礼もまだだし、桜に挨拶してこよう。
contexts.english: I haven't thanked Sakura for cooking dinner yet, so I should talk to Sakura.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page1:1
contexts.japanese: 「そうだな。夜も遅いし、家まで送っていってやらないと」
contexts.english: "It's getting late, so I should walk her home."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page2:1
contexts.japanese: 居間では後片づけを済ませ、帰り支度をしている桜がいた。
contexts.english: Sakura just finished cleaning up, and she's in the living room getting ready to go home.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page3:1
contexts.japanese: 「あれ、先輩。お風呂に入ってたんじゃないんですか？」
contexts.english: "Oh, Senpai. I thought you were taking your bath."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page3:1
contexts.japanese: 「いや、風呂は後回し。桜を送ってから入る」
contexts.english: "I'll take my bath later, after I walk you home."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page3:1
contexts.japanese: 「え……送るって、わたしをですか？」
contexts.english: "Eh? You're going to walk...me home?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page4:1
contexts.japanese: 「ああ。最近物騒だから家まで送る。桜ん家、けっこう遠いだろう。わざわざ来て貰ってるんだから、それぐらいはさせてくれ」
contexts.english: "Yeah. It's been dangerous at night lately so I'll walk you home. Your house is a pretty long walk, so let me at least do this, since you go out of your way to come here."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page4:1
contexts.japanese: 桜は気まずそうに口を閉ざす。
contexts.english: Sakura purses her lips awkwardly.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page4:1
contexts.japanese: ……なにかまずい事でも口にしたんだろうか、俺。
contexts.english: ...Did I say something wrong?

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page5:1
contexts.japanese: 「……ごめんなさい。気持ちは嬉しいんですけど、先輩は休んでいてください。家までだったら慣れてますし、一人でも大丈夫ですから」
contexts.english: "I'm sorry. I appreciate your concern, but you should rest. I know my way home from here, and I should be fine alone."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page6:1
contexts.japanese: 「いや、それはそうだろうけど、今日は特別だ。しばらくは家まで送っていくよ」
contexts.english: "Maybe so, but today's special. I'll walk you home at night for a while."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page6:1
contexts.japanese: 「……でも、その……兄さんに見つかると、先輩にまで迷惑がかかります」
contexts.english: "...But, well...it will cause trouble for you if my brother sees you."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page8:1
contexts.japanese: いや、慎二がなんと言おうが、こんな物騒な時に桜を一人で帰らせる方が問題じゃないか。
contexts.english: No matter what Shinji might say, letting Sakura go home alone during these dangerous times would be much worse.

counterexamples.description: Sakura worries about imposing; Shirou cites her daily help, confidence in a fight and his promise to protect her.
counterexamples.sourceReading: These are Shirou's judgments, not objective guarantees.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura worries about imposing; Shirou cites her daily help, confidence in a fight and his promise to protect her.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page9:1
contexts.japanese: 「あの、でも、やっぱり先輩に悪いですから、その」
contexts.english: "Um, but I would hate for you to go out of your way, so..."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page10:1
contexts.japanese: 「え……いえ、そういうコトではなくて、ですね」
contexts.english: "Eh...um, well that's not exactly what I meant..."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page10:1
contexts.japanese: 「ならいいだろ。これでも腕には自信があるんだ。たいていの暴漢は返り討ちに出来るから、こんな時ぐらいは使ってやってくれ。なんか出てきてもちゃんと桜を守るから」
contexts.english: "That settles it then. I'm pretty confident in my skills. I think I can deal with any ordinary attacker, so you should make use of me at times like this. I'll protect you, no matter what."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page10:1
contexts.japanese: ほら、と視線で桜を廊下へ促す。
contexts.english: I nudge Sakura towards the hallway with a glance.

counterexamples.description: Sakura warns of another argument; Shirou says direct conflict clears his own feelings but may make Shinji feel worse.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The scene does not certify fighting as safe for Shinji.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura warns of another argument; Shirou says direct conflict clears his own feelings but may make Shinji feel worse.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page11:1
contexts.japanese: 「先輩……？　ホントにいいんですか？　また兄さんとケンカ、しちゃうかもしれませんよ」
contexts.english: "Senpai? Are you sure about this? You might have another argument with my brother."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page11:1
contexts.japanese: あいつ、ああ見えて隠し事とか嫌いだから。文句があるならすっぱりと言い合った方がスッキリする」
contexts.english: He may not show it, but he hates when people hide things from him. If he and I have something to complain about, it's best we get it off our chests."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page11:1
contexts.japanese: なぜか、桜は驚いた顔をする。
contexts.english: Sakura looks surprised for some reason.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page12:1
contexts.japanese: 「どした？　なんかヘンなコト言ったか、俺」
contexts.english: "What's wrong? Did I say something weird?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page12:1
contexts.japanese: 「いえ、言ってませんよ。先輩が兄さんと仲良くしてくれるのが嬉しいだけです」
contexts.english: "No, no. I'm just glad you're friendly with my brother."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page12:1
contexts.japanese: 「？　いや、仲良くってのは難しいぞ。スッキリするのは俺だけで、慎二は逆かもしれないし」
contexts.english: "Really? Actually, calling it friendly might be a bit of a stretch. I'm the only one who feels better after our spats; Shinji might feel the opposite."

counterexamples.description: Sakura's paradoxical account says Shinji dislikes Shirou yet attends to him because he likes him more than others; she then admits teasing from envy.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The object and cause of envy are not explained beyond her words.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura's paradoxical account says Shinji dislikes Shirou yet attends to him because he likes him more than others; she then admits teasing from envy.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 「そうですね。けど兄さん、何度ケンカしても先輩に話しかけるでしょう？　兄さん、きっと先輩が苦手なんです。けど他の人よりずっと好きだから、いつも先輩を気にしてるんですよ。素直じゃない人だから、嫌いな人が好きなんです、兄さん」
contexts.english: "You may be right. But have you noticed my brother still speaks to you no matter how many times you two fight? I have a feeling he does not get along with you, but he still likes you more than most, and that's why he's always mindful of you. He doesn't wear his heart on his sleeve, and he likes people he dislikes."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page14:1
contexts.japanese: 「……えっと。それは、返答に困る意見だな」
contexts.english: "...Um, I really don't know how to respond to that."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page14:1
contexts.japanese: 「はい。先輩が羨ましかったから、少しだけ困らせてみました」
contexts.english: "Well, I'm a bit jealous of you, so I wanted to say something that might make you a little uncomfortable."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page14:1
contexts.japanese: にっこりと笑う桜。
contexts.english: Sakura smiles gently.

counterexamples.description: Shirou is arrested by Sakura's full smile, predicts Shinji may accept the escort, and Sakura tentatively agrees that openness may be better.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Prediction and agreement remain qualified.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou is arrested by Sakura's full smile, predicts Shinji may accept the escort, and Sakura tentatively agrees that openness may be better.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page15:1
contexts.japanese: 「ぁ—ぅ」

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page15:1
contexts.japanese: その笑顔に、知らず息を呑んでいた。
contexts.english: Seeing her smile makes my breath catch in my throat.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page15:1
contexts.japanese: 満面の笑顔というのか。
contexts.english: It's like she's beaming.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page15:1
contexts.japanese: あんなふうに桜が笑うの、初めて見た気がする。
contexts.english: I think this is the first time I've seen Sakura smile like that.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page16:1
contexts.japanese: 「と、とにかく送っていくからな。慎二に見つかったら見つかったでいい。妹を送り届けたんだから、あいつだって文句は言わないだろ」
contexts.english: "A-anyway, I'm going to walk you home. I don't care if Shinji sees us. He shouldn't have anything to complain about since I'm just walking his sister home."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page17:1
contexts.japanese: 「そうですね。隠すよりはそうした方がいいかもしれません。それじゃお言葉に甘えていいですか、先輩」
contexts.english: "You're right. It might be better that way rather than hiding it. Okay, I accept your offer, Senpai."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page17:1
contexts.japanese: 「あいよ。たまには先輩らしいトコ見せてやる」
contexts.english: "Got it. I should act like your elder once in a while, you know."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page17:1
contexts.japanese: とん、と胸を叩く。
contexts.english: I pound my chest to demonstrate my determination.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page17:1
contexts.japanese: 任せとけ、という意思表示に、桜は温かそうな笑顔で頷いていた。
contexts.english: Sakura nods with a smile when she sees my conviction.

counterexamples.description: Before ten, the abnormally empty route leads to Sakura correcting the location of the Matou and Tohsaka homes.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Matou is high on the hill; Tohsaka is at the top.
counterexamples.explanation: Before ten, the abnormally empty route leads to Sakura correcting the location of the Matou and Tohsaka homes.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page18:1
contexts.japanese: 坂道を下りて、交差点に到着する。
contexts.english: We walk downhill and reach the intersection.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page18:1
contexts.japanese: あたりに人影はなく、見慣れた住宅地はひどく寂しく感じられた。
contexts.english: There's no one else around, and the familiar residential area feels oddly desolate.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page19:1
contexts.japanese: まだ十時前だというのに、町は完全に眠りについている。
contexts.english: It's only a little before ten o'clock, but the entire town is sleeping.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page19:1
contexts.japanese: ……その静けさは、どこか異常だ。
contexts.english: ...The silence feels unnatural.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page19:1
contexts.japanese: 物騒な事件が続いているとは言え、夜というものはここまで活気を奪うものだったか。
contexts.english: It may have to do with all the recent incidents, but it's hard to believe the town could lose so much spirit just because it's dark out.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 「先輩……？　あの、わたしの家こっちですけど」
contexts.english: "Senpai? Um, my home is this way."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 「え？　ああ、悪い、ちょっとぼうっとしてた。桜の家はあっち側の一番上だもんな」
contexts.english: "Eh? Oh, sorry. I got distracted. Your house is at the very top of that path."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page20:1
contexts.japanese: 「いえ、一番上にあるのは遠坂先輩のお家ですよ。間桐の家も高いところにありますけど、一番上じゃないんです」
contexts.english: "No, the house at the very top is Miss Tohsaka's home. The Matou home may be high up, but not that high."

counterexamples.description: Sakura asks whether Rin is difficult for Shirou; he limits his knowledge to her conspicuous school reputation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The old greeting does not become an intimate relationship.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura asks whether Rin is difficult for Shirou; he limits his knowledge to her conspicuous school reputation.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page21:1
contexts.japanese: 「あれ、そうだったか？　……って、遠坂ってあの遠坂……？」
contexts.english: "It isn't? Hey wait, is Tohsaka...THE Tohsaka?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page21:1
contexts.japanese: 「はい、二年生の遠坂凛さんです。先輩、苦手なんですか？」
contexts.english: "That's right. Miss Rin Tohsaka, the second year. Do you not get along with her?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page21:1
contexts.japanese: こっちの心情を察したのか、桜は的確なつっこみをする。
contexts.english: Sakura speaks as if she read my mind.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page21:1
contexts.japanese: むむ……そんなに苦い顔してたのか、俺。
contexts.english: Ugh. Was I really so obvious?

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page22:1
contexts.japanese: 「いや、苦手ってワケじゃない。話した事もないし、よく知らない相手だ。ただ有名な優等生だろ、あいつ。何処にいても目立つから、人並みに知ってるだけ」
contexts.english: "Well, it's not that I don't get along with her... I don't really talk to her in the first place. I just don't really know her. She's just a popular honor student. She stands out, so I only know as much about her as anyone else."

counterexamples.description: The nearby Western homes lead into childhood rumors of a scary magician, which Sakura once took seriously.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The rumor is not converted into current proof of the setting's formal magic system.
counterexamples.explanation: The nearby Western homes lead into childhood rumors of a scary magician, which Sakura once took seriously.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page23:1
contexts.japanese: 「そういう桜は？　同じ洋館だし、もしかして近所づきあいとかあるのか？」
contexts.english: "What about you? You two both live in Western houses in the same neighborhood, so do you ever talk?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page23:1
contexts.japanese: 「ないですよ。たしかに近所ではありますけど、遠坂先輩のお家は坂の上ですから。
contexts.english: "We do not. We may live close to each other, but Miss Tohsaka's home is higher up on the hill.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page23:1
contexts.japanese: けど、遠坂先輩のお家が洋館だって知ってるんですね、先輩」
contexts.english: But how did you know Miss Tohsaka's home is a Western house?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page24:1
contexts.japanese: 「ああ、ちょっと小耳に挟んだんだ。遠坂んところは幽霊屋敷だとかなんとか。幽霊屋敷っていったら洋館と相場が決まってるだろ」
contexts.english: "I heard a rumor about Tohsaka's house being a haunted mansion or something. And you would think a haunted mansion would be more of a Western house."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page25:1
contexts.japanese: 「そうですね。遠坂先輩は一人が好きみたいですから。わたしも子供の頃、坂の上には怖い魔法使いが住んでるって言われてました」
contexts.english: "You're right. I believe Miss Tohsaka likes to keep to herself, and when I was little, I was told that there was a scary magician living on top of the hill."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page26:1
contexts.japanese: 「へえ、怖い魔法使いか。俺もそんなふうな噂は聞いたな。まあ、それ言ったら洋館側の家はみんな魔法使いが住んでいそうだけど。で、桜は信じたのか、その話？」
contexts.english: "A scary magician, huh? I think I heard that rumor too. Though, all the Western houses on that side of town seem like there would be magicians living in them. So did you believe those rumors, Sakura?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page27:1
contexts.japanese: 「信じました。だって子供だったんです。だから、坂の上には行っちゃいけないって、いつも思ってました」
contexts.english: "I did. I was a child, after all. That's why I always avoided going all the way up the hill."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page27:1
contexts.japanese: 面白半分で聞いたコトに、桜は真剣な顔で答えていた。
contexts.english: I was only asking half-jokingly, but her response seems to have been in earnest.

counterexamples.description: The opposite residential slope has similar layout, fewer buildings and more unmanaged woods; Matou is one of the few homes near the top.
counterexamples.sourceReading: It is not moved above the Tohsaka house.
counterexamples.explanation: The opposite residential slope has similar layout, fewer buildings and more unmanaged woods; Matou is one of the few homes near the top.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page28:1
contexts.japanese: 坂道を上っていく。
contexts.english: We walk up the hill.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page28:1
contexts.japanese: うちの方とは正反対の住宅地だが、その在り方は変わらない。
contexts.english: The residential area here may be on the opposite side of town from where I live, but its layout is similar.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page29:1
contexts.japanese: 坂道は上って行けば行くほど建物が少なくなり、人の手が入っていない雑木林が多くなる。
contexts.english: The higher you go up the hill, the fewer buildings there are, and the denser the thickets of trees grow.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page29:1
contexts.japanese: その中で、頂上に近い位置にある数少ない建物が桜の家、間桐邸だ。
contexts.english: And one of the few buildings near the top of the hill is Sakura's house, the Matou residence.

counterexamples.description: Sakura asks about a recently recurring stranger near home, but no figure is visible now.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Present absence and prior sightings remain distinct.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura asks about a recently recurring stranger near home, but no figure is visible now.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page30:1
contexts.english: "Oh."

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page30:1
contexts.japanese: 不意に桜が立ち止まった。
contexts.english: Sakura suddenly stops.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page30:1
contexts.japanese: 「ん？　なんだ、忘れ物か？」
contexts.english: "Hm? What's wrong? Did you forget something?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page30:1
contexts.japanese: 「ぁ……いえ、忘れ物じゃないんですけど……先輩、うちの近くに誰かいませんか？」
contexts.english: "No, I didn't forget anything...but do you see someone near my home?"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-14:page30:1
contexts.japanese: 不安そうにあたりの様子を窺う桜。
contexts.english: Sakura peers ahead, looking concerned.
